analysis.session_summary: The tape was catalyst-light: apart from NZD CPI q/q, no leg had high confidence, and most major pairs chopped without a clean driver. JPY was the standout winner, finishing up 0.627% strength and driving USD/JPY down 116.2 pips, while NZD was weakest after CPI q/q missed at 0.7% vs 0.8%. The US Unemployment Claims beat (194K vs 200K) was muted, moving the USD basket only 0.019% and not producing follow-through. Risk proxies firmed—VIX +4.837% and USD/ZAR +0.923%—but G10 FX stayed rangebound.

themes.evidence: EUR/USD legs all confidence none; only NZD CPI had a high-confidence leg.
NZD CPI q/q 0.7% vs forecast 0.8%; own-ccy impulse -0.124%; NZD/USD -16.4 pips.
JPY strength_pct 0.627; USD/JPY -116.2 pips; CHF/JPY -81.0 pips.

currency_drivers.CHF: No catalyst; held range, gained modestly as risk hedge.
currency_drivers.NZD: CPI q/q miss at 0.7% vs 0.8% drove initial drop; later moves lacked catalysts.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD printed four catalyst-less legs; the largest down leg from 05:00 to 16:15 (-62.3 pips) coincided only with noise, and the close sat 0.53 in range.

polarity_reads.read: Miss produced normal polarity (NZD -0.124%), implying no downside cushion or inverted positioning.
Beat was muted at 0.019% inside noise despite 194K vs 200K, showing limited fresh USD demand or already stretched longs.
